commits.messageBody:
…gle re-approval

Five open pull requests changed this one document: #2392 (the Clarify
selections), #2311, #2344 and #2385 (three approvals of the text those
selections change), and #2303 (a drain-written rewrite). Issue #2391 named a
false statement in it. This is the one text that replaces them.

What changed from the text on main (canonical hash 04311d22...545f, the hash
all three approval records carry):

- Clarify selections for CQ-1, CQ-2 and CQ-3, carried from #2392 word for word.
- The config-blind measurement corrected (#2391). Re-measured at 901fea36: the
  shipped VALIDATE_PY template has 5 occurrences of config.json and 1 of
  import json, this repository's copy has none, and neither names specsDir or
  decisionsDir. The template has read the config for ownershipDeclaration
  since #2264.
- FR-2's reach stated: one config read and one outcome for the whole script.
  The shipped ownership read warns and carries on for the same file
  (template-registry.ts:1890-1895), and shipped-ownership-gate-2250.test.ts:284-290
  pins that with exit 0, which AC-4 as approved reverses. Recorded as CQ-5;
  FR-1 loses the word "unreadable"; AC-7 is new; the test is declared under
  affects: before approval.
- What the spec does not close is said outright, taken from #2303: a corpus
  mapped to one frontmatter key cannot express the cross-field check #1698
  lost. Recorded as CQ-4, with the cost of not taking CQ-2 option c.
- An opening paragraph that carries the decision, and a "Changes since the
  approved text" section.

Not carried from #2303: the refresh half. It widens the approved scope to a
second mechanism and every managed-region template, and brings three
unanswered questions, one of them a tracked-format choice reserved for the
founder. Tracked as #2615.

No approval record and no status or phases change: approval is the founder's
act, made afterwards on this text. status stays specifying.

npm run validate: exit 0, 0 FAIL, 182 WARN, identical to origin/main.
npx vitest run: 359 files, 7954 tests passed.

…ved into the changes section

The founder reads only the opening paragraph, and at about 330 words he would
not. It now says four things: what he is approving, that his approval of
2026-10-01 does not carry over because an approval is tied to the exact text,
the one cost that bites (a broken config file blocks commits), and that nothing
is left for him to answer.

Every other fact the old paragraph carried is now in "Changes since the
approved text": the three earlier Clarify answers in plain words, the #2264
timing, FR-2's new reach, what the spec does not fix, both costs under "What
approving costs", and a table of the five recorded choices with the cost of
each. No requirement, acceptance criterion, invariant or recorded selection
changes in this commit.

Pre-flight of the approval itself, replayed headlessly against this file with
the extension's own library functions (commands/approve.ts:237-384): opt-in
marker, picker, validateSpec, violationsIntroducedByApproval and approver
identity all accept. Controls refuse: the same file without its implements:
line (ownership.implements.missing), without acceptance criteria
(acceptance.missing), and the bot identity. With the old approval record
(hash 04311d22...) beside the new text the status reads stale, the picker
still offers the spec, and the write records the new hash and reads approved.

npm run validate: exit 0, 0 FAIL, 182 WARN, identical to origin/main.

…" and re-reads citations at 1bc9e484

"Why no new DR" named only the choice to extend by configuration. It now
names the second choice FR-2 makes (a config file that is present and cannot
be read or parsed fails the whole shipped script) and gives the reasons that
choice is put to approval in this spec and not in a record of its own:

- FR-2, AC-4 and INV-1 are byte-identical to the text approved on 2026-10-01,
  and AC-4 cannot be built without changing
  shipped-ownership-gate-2250.test.ts:284-290
- invariant 2 and DR-066 set the direction, though not alone
- the leniency it replaces came in with #2264 as a docstring, a comment and
  one test case; SPEC-038's text is silent on it and no decision record
  decides it (DR-099's Context describes it)
- returning to a warning later breaks no project

It also says what the spec leaves to #1687 and #2001, which both recommend
something softer than FR-2, and that a reader who wants a decision record
should say so before approving.

No requirement, acceptance criterion or invariant changes. Line citations
that lagged main are re-read at 1bc9e484: template-registry.ts had moved by
2 to 59 lines, and the loadConfig fallback is config.ts:214-216.

Answers the ai-review architect finding on #2617.
